_comment: Weekly power-ranking blurbs. The scheduled job appends one object to weeks[] after each week finalizes, in the same pass that writes recaps.json. The site computes the ranking itself and only reads the one-line blurbs from here — if this file is missing, empty, or has nothing for the week being viewed, the board still renders with each team's record and points instead.

teams[].manager: manager display name, exactly as Sleeper spells it
teams[].blurb: one sentence, ESPN house style. No score recaps - those live in recaps.json. Say something about the team's week or where it is heading.

teams.blurb: Opened with 195.9 and spread it across the lineup rather than leaning on one player, then left another 54 points on the bench without needing them.
Caleb Williams' 37.26 was the best single number of the week, and it came in the highest-scoring game anyone played.
Kenneth Walker's 35.6 did the heavy lifting in a game where both benches outscored the margin several times over.
Won the tightest game of the week without a second big score, which is a harder way to do it than the scoreboard suggests.
Derrick Henry carried nearly a third of the total and a starting tight end on zero cost nothing.
Took the quietest game on the slate with 105.2 and picked up Christian McCaffrey in the preseason, though not for long.
Scored 161.86, more than three of the six winners managed, and has nothing to show for it.
Traded three times before a ball was snapped, ended up with McCaffrey after all, and still lost while 44.9 sat on his bench.
125.1 would have been competitive in four of the other games; it arrived against the week's high score instead.
Had Josh Allen's 35.66, the best performance on the losing side all week, and 43.6 more sitting unused.
Lost by 14.46 with 53.64 on the bench, which is the kind of week that looks worse on the lineup sheet than the scoreboard.
The week's lowest score at 90.5, with one player in double figures and 35.36 left behind.
